nodes.description: POPDC3 is the POPDC1 paralogue, also a plasma-membrane cAMP-binding protein of striated muscle. The only functional readout reported for the three LGMD R26 variants is aberrant modulation of the mechano-gated potassium channel TREK-1 in Xenopus oocytes. No source reports a membrane-trafficking defect for POPDC3, and the path from altered TREK-1 modulation to the sarcolemmal lesion is not established, so this node is kept separate from the POPDC1 trafficking node and its downstream link names no intermediate step. POPDC3 disease, in the reported patients, did not involve the heart.

evidence.reference_title: POPDC3 Gene Variants Associate with a New Form of Limb Girdle Muscular Dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: All 3 mutants cloned in Xenopus oocytes caused an aberrant modulation of the mechano-gated potassium channel, TREK-1.

nodes.description: Alpha-dystroglycan reaches the extracellular matrix only after an O-mannosyl glycan is phosphorylated and then extended by LARGE; the mature glycan is what binds laminin with high affinity. Two of the LGMD-R genes act inside this pathway rather than on the sarcolemmal complex itself. DAG1 is the substrate: the Thr192Met variant blocks LARGE-dependent maturation of the phosphorylated O-mannosyl glycan, so the receptor loses laminin binding despite being present. POMK is the kinase that performs the phosphorylation step, and truncating alleles that remove its kinase domain produce dystroglycanopathy ranging from Walker-Warburg syndrome to limb-girdle weakness with cognitive defects. This node is the primary-dystroglycanopathy counterpart of the FKRP-driven secondary dystroglycanopathy recorded on the sarcolemmal node below.
nodes.id: Alpha-Dystroglycan Hypoglycosylation and Loss of Laminin Binding

evidence.reference_title: A dystroglycan mutation associated with limb-girdle muscular dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: In vitro and in vivo studies showed that the mutation impairs the receptor function of dystroglycan in skeletal muscle and brain by inhibiting the post-translational modification, mediated by the glycosyltransferase LARGE, of the phosphorylated O-mannosyl glycans on α-dystroglycan that is required for high-affinity binding to laminin.

evidence.reference_title: POMK mutations disrupt muscle development leading to a spectrum of neuromuscular presentations.
evidence.snippet: POMK, which was found mutated in two dystroglycanopathy cases, is instead involved in a glycan phosphorylation reaction critical for ECM binding, but little is known about the clinical presentation of POMK mutations or of the function of this protein in the muscle.

evidence.reference_title: POMK mutations disrupt muscle development leading to a spectrum of neuromuscular presentations.
evidence.snippet: Analysis of loss of function in the zebrafish embryo and larva showed that pomk function is necessary for normal muscle development, leading to locomotor dysfuction in the embryo and signs of muscular dystrophy in the larva.

nodes.description: Calpain-3 is the muscle-specific calcium-dependent protease, held at the N2A region of titin in the sarcomere and activated by sustained modest rises in cytoplasmic calcium such as those following eccentric contraction. Loss of calpain-3 expression causes LGMDR1, and its pathogenic mechanism is understood as impaired sarcomere remodelling rather than as sarcolemmal fragility, which is why this subtype is wired to a separate node from the sarcoglycanopathies and dysferlinopathy.
nodes.id: Calpain-3 Deficiency and Impaired Sarcomere Remodelling

evidence.reference_title: Calpains, skeletal muscle function and exercise.
evidence.snippet: The physiological roles of the calpains are not well understood, although ubiquitous calpains have been associated with apoptosis and myogenesis and calpain-3 is likely involved in sarcomeric remodelling. A defect in the expression of calpain-3 results in limb-girdle muscular dystrophy Type 2A.

evidence.reference_title: Calpains, skeletal muscle function and exercise.
evidence.snippet: Calpain-3 is tightly bound in skeletal muscle fibres at the N2A line of the large elastic protein titin.

evidence.reference_title: Muscle atrophy in Limb Girdle Muscular Dystrophy 2A: a morphometric and molecular study.
evidence.snippet: The peculiar clinical features and the pathogenic mechanism related to calpain-3 deficiency (impaired sarcomere remodelling) suggest that the ubiquitin-proteasome degradation pathway may have a crucial role in Limb Girdle Muscular Dystrophy 2A (LGMD2A).

nodes.description: Sustained injury drives chronic inflammation (with impaired macrophage M1-to-M2 switching) and progressive replacement of contractile muscle by fibrotic and adipose tissue, which is detectable as subtype-specific fatty infiltration patterns on muscle MRI and as fibrosis on biopsy. This is the structural substrate of permanent weakness.

nodes.description: TRAPPC11 is a subunit of the multiprotein TRAPP membrane-trafficking complex. Both reported LGMD R18 alleles weaken TRAPPC11 binding to other TRAPP components and disrupt Golgi architecture. Endoplasmic-reticulum-to-Golgi transport remains normal while exit from the Golgi to the cell surface is dramatically delayed, and the lysosomal membrane glycoproteins LAMP1 and LAMP2 are altered as a consequence, so the defect is in secretory-pathway transit rather than in the sarcolemmal complex.

nodes.description: POPDC1 is a plasma-membrane cAMP-binding protein abundant in striated muscle. The LGMD2X variant POPDC1 S201F halves cAMP affinity and, in patient skeletal muscle, leaves both mutant POPDC1 and wild-type POPDC2 stranded short of the membrane. POPDC1 disease carries cardiac arrhythmia. The paralogue POPDC3 is modelled separately: no source reports a trafficking defect for it, so it is not listed on this node.

nodes.description: Two LGMD-R genes act on the Notch pathway rather than on the sarcolemma: POGLUT1 O-glucosylates Notch, and JAG2 encodes the Notch ligand Jagged2. Muscle from POGLUT1 patients shows reduced Notch signalling, and restoring Notch signalling rescues the myogenic defect in their primary myoblasts. JAG2 muscle shows misregulation of myogenesis genes including PAX7. This node holds the pathway state; its cellular consequence is recorded separately on the satellite cell node it points at, because the sources treat the two as cause and effect.

nodes.description: Across LGMD-R subtypes the proximate defect destabilizes the myofiber plasma membrane (sarcolemma). Sarcoglycanopathies (SGCA-D) and dystroglycanopathies (FKRP) disrupt the dystrophin-glycoprotein complex that links the cytoskeleton to the extracellular matrix, while dysferlin (DYSF) deficiency impairs calcium-triggered resealing of membrane microtears. The result is a fragile sarcolemma that cannot withstand or repair contraction-induced injury.

evidence.snippet: A specific subgroup of muscular dystrophies is associated with genetic defects in components of the dystrophin-glycoprotein complex (DGC), which plays a crucial role in linking the cytosol to the skeletal muscle basement membrane. In these cases, dystrophin-associated proteins fail to correctly localize to the sarcolemma

nodes.description: Skeletal muscle regeneration depends on satellite cells, whose quiescence and self-renewal are controlled by Notch signalling. POGLUT1 patients' muscle holds a dramatically reduced satellite cell pool, and their primary myoblasts proliferate slowly, differentiate too readily, and hold a smaller pool of quiescent PAX7-positive cells. The authors name Notch-dependent loss of satellite cells as the pathomechanism, which is why this node sits downstream of the pathway node rather than beside it.

evidence.reference_title: A POGLUT1 mutation causes a muscular dystrophy with reduced Notch signaling and satellite cell loss.
evidence.snippet: These data suggest that a key pathomechanism for this novel form of muscular dystrophy is Notch-dependent loss of satellite cells.
